headline: Microsoft is directly named in Collins's question citing a CMA decision of 14 May 2026 and in Mishra's question about the 13 November outage, alongside questions on software lock-in. Collins also invoked "the Microsoft outage" during the Commons debate on the Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill to press ministers on digital sovereignty and reliance on foreign suppliers.
summary: The supplied material highlights government supplier dependency: Collins asked about a CMA decision to investigate Microsoft's business software ecosystem, MPs questioned software lock-in and exit costs, and Mishra sought an assessment of the Microsoft outage's impact on Parliament. During Commons consideration of Lords amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill on 24 November, Collins invoked the outage, while MPs also raised AI "loss of control" risk and sovereign cloud capability. Separately, civil service pension problems involving Capita, teachers' pension administration-transfer problems, Palantir's government contracts, the draft National Policy Statement for Data Centres consultation and AI-cyber investment feature in the supplied records. Today (25 November 2026) brings a scheduled Westminster Hall debate on driverless vehicle regulation and Grand Committee consideration of subscription-contract rules.

very_important.title: Collins invokes "the Microsoft outage" and MPs raise digital sovereignty in Cyber Security and Resilience Bill debate
very_important.who: Victoria Collins MP (Liberal Democrat, Harpenden and Berkhamsted); Dame Chi Onwurah MP (Labour, Newcastle upon Tyne Central and West); Mark Pritchard MP (Conservative, The Wrekin); Ian Murray MP (Minister)
very_important.where: House of Commons Chamber — Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill (consideration of Lords amendments)
very_important.body: During debate on Lords amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill, Victoria Collins explicitly referenced "the Microsoft outage" when asking ministers what assessment had been made of government and public-service reliance on foreign technology suppliers, and pressed for clarity on the AI sovereign wealth fund and the UK's digital sovereignty strategy. Dame Chi Onwurah discussed the Hugging Face AI "loss of control" incident and Anthropic's valuation, arguing Lords amendment 33 focused too narrowly on buyers rather than AI developers. Mark Pritchard raised UK/EU "sovereign cloud capability" versus US big tech, and Minister Ian Murray responded on vendor lock-in, the national cloud infrastructure project and the AI sovereign wealth fund.
very_important.why: Microsoft is named directly in connection with outage risk and dependency on foreign suppliers, and the exchange touches digital sovereignty, AI safety/loss-of-control and cyber resilience.
very_important.linkText: Hansard: Cyber Security and Resilience Bill debate

very_important.title: Question citing CMA investigation into "Microsoft's business software ecosystem" and open-source/exit questions
very_important.who: Victoria Collins MP (Liberal Democrat, Harpenden and Berkhamsted)
very_important.where: Written questions — Cabinet Office and Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
very_important.body: Collins asked DCMS about the policy implications of a CMA decision, dated 14 May 2026, to open a strategic market status investigation into "Microsoft's business software ecosystem" (uin 46042). She also asked about a possible publicly owned body to develop and maintain open-source software for the public sector (uin 46039) and open-source alternatives to productivity/collaboration software used by central government (uin 46040). Separately she asked the Cabinet Office what assessment it has made of the risks of single-supplier government software, contingency plans for loss of access to services from suppliers headquartered outside the UK, and the adequacy of exit and data-portability provisions in cloud/productivity contracts (uin 46038). No answers to these questions are supplied.
very_important.why: Connects a question about Microsoft's business software ecosystem with questions about open-source alternatives, government software dependency and exit planning.
very_important.linkText: Written question 46042: Microsoft's business software ecosystem (CMA investigation)

very_important.title: Government software-switching costs and provider lock-in questioned
very_important.who: Martin Wrigley MP (Liberal Democrat, Newton Abbot)
very_important.where: Written questions — Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
very_important.body: Wrigley asked DCMS about the impact of current contracts on public bodies' ability to switch software providers (uin 46025), whether it has changed its main software provider in the past 10 years (uin 46026), and whether it has estimated the cost of changing its main provider or plans to assess its software estate and establish a dedicated Software Asset Management system (uin 46028).
very_important.why: Addresses switching costs, contractual barriers to changing providers and software-asset management.

very_important.title: Mishra asks about Microsoft outage impact on Parliament; Hollinrake separately raises website performance
very_important.who: Navendu Mishra MP (Labour, Stockport); Kevin Hollinrake MP (Conservative, Thirsk and Malton)
very_important.where: Written questions — House of Commons Commission
very_important.body: Mishra asked whether the Commons Commission has assessed the impact of the global Microsoft outage on 13 November 2026 on Parliamentary Digital Services (uin 46113). Hollinrake separately asked what is being done to improve the reliability of the questions-statements.parliament.uk website, including preventing error messages and improving response times (uin 46129).
very_important.why: Requests an assessment of possible outage effects on Parliamentary Digital Services and separately raises questions-website performance; no answers or confirmed outage effects on Parliament are supplied.
very_important.linkText: Written question 46113: Microsoft outage impact on Parliamentary Digital Services

very_important.title: Civil Service Pension Scheme urgent question: Capita failures and insourcing
very_important.who: Lisa Smart MP (Liberal Democrat); Sally Jameson MP (Minister, Cabinet Office)
very_important.where: House of Commons Chamber — Urgent Question
very_important.body: Lisa Smart pressed the Minister on Capita's performance administering the Civil Service Pension Scheme. Minister Sally Jameson confirmed the Procurement Act 2023 gives government debarment powers over poorly performing suppliers, but declined to confirm or deny whether any supplier was under investigation. She also set out the Government's insourcing commitments, referring to the insourcing unit and the forthcoming public interest test.
very_important.why: Sets out the minister's position on poor-performance debarment powers and insourcing. She did not confirm an investigation into Capita or promise immediate insourcing.
very_important.linkText: Hansard: Civil Service Pension Scheme urgent question

very_important.title: National Policy Statement for Data Centres consultation (closes 8 January 2027)
very_important.who: Clive Lewis MP (Labour, Norwich South); Kanishka Narayan MP (Minister)
very_important.where: Written question — Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
very_important.body: Lewis asked whether private companies were consulted on the draft National Policy Statement for Data Centres. The Minister confirmed the draft NPS was published for consultation on 28 October 2026, engaging developers, local authorities, trade bodies and environmental groups, with the consultation closing on 8 January 2027.
very_important.why: A planning-policy consultation with an evidenced deadline, concerning the framework for future data-centre development.
very_important.linkText: Written question 44886: National Policy Statement for Data Centres consultation

very_important.title: Government AI-cyber defence investment: frontier-AI pilots, Cyber Shield and the National Agentic Security Unit
very_important.who: Viscount Camrose (Conservative, Shadow Minister Cabinet Office for AI and Cyber); Lord Sarfraz (Conservative)
very_important.where: Written questions — Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
very_important.body: Viscount Camrose questioned the token-use and cost allocation of a frontier-AI model pilot for government (HL5143, HL5144), and responsibility for the National Agentic Security Unit (HL5141). The answer on the unit said the Autumn Budget announced £40 million for it, that it was being established by NCSC and DCMS, and that it would be housed within NCSC, part of GCHQ, to detect, investigate and respond to agentic-AI incidents. Lord Sarfraz asked about reports that automated software, including AI agents, accounts for the majority of web traffic; the answer confirmed £60 million for "Cyber Shield" (agentic AI for cyber defence), £70 million for a National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre, and the £40 million National Agentic Security Unit.
very_important.why: Concerns government investment in AI-assisted cyber defence and frontier-AI pilots, without establishing involvement by any particular commercial supplier.
very_important.linkText: Written question HL5326: AI agents, web traffic and the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill

debates.title: COP31 statement: opposition to Larbert hyperscale AI data centre
debates.who: Brian Leishman MP (Labour, Alloa and Grangemouth)
debates.where: House of Commons Chamber — COP31 statement
debates.body: During the COP31 statement, Leishman said constituents in Larbert were campaigning against a proposed hyperscale AI data centre in a residential area near a care home and hospital. He raised climate and community concerns about the proposed development.
debates.why: Highlights a constituency-level campaign over a proposed AI data centre's proximity to homes and public services.
debates.linkText: Hansard: COP31 statement — Larbert data centre

questions.title: Dr Ben Spencer's sustained scrutiny of the Prime Minister's AI Taskforce and government AI strategy
questions.who: Dr Ben Spencer MP (Conservative, Runnymede and Weybridge)
questions.where: Written questions — Cabinet Office; Department for Transport; Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office; Treasury
questions.body: A long series of questions pressed on the Prime Minister's AI Taskforce (based in the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet, chaired by Lord Vallance): what projects and priorities it has set, whether milestones have been set, whether it has a role in departmental AI-supplier choices, and whether a single document defines AI responsibilities across government (uin 44763, 44904, 44906, 44907, 44911, 44916, 46350, 46356, 46364, 46366). Separately, 44431 asks whether the National Security Unit for Procurement has assessed suppliers of AI models and services to government. Spencer also asked several departments (Transport, FCDO, Treasury) whether they use any open-weight AI model published by a developer based in China (uin 46361, 46363, 44449 — Treasury confirmed it does not).
questions.why: Sustained opposition scrutiny of the machinery and direction of UK government AI strategy and of Chinese AI model use in government, both central to the AI regulation/sovereignty theme.
questions.linkText: Written question 44763: lessons from the Vaccines Taskforce for the AI Taskforce

questions.title: Palantir's government contracts questioned across departments
questions.who: Clive Lewis MP (Labour, Norwich South); Martin Wrigley MP (Liberal Democrat, Newton Abbot)
questions.where: Written questions — Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office; Ministry of Defence; Department of Health and Social Care
questions.body: Lewis asked the FCDO about policy implications in a question citing exits from contracts or exclusion of Palantir from bidding in France, Switzerland and the German army on national security grounds (uin 44199), and asked DHSC to publish its agreement with Palantir for the NHS Federated Data Platform (uin 44885). Wrigley asked the MoD whether it would reassess its use of Palantir (uin 44056); the Minister said the MoD "continually reviews" its technology arrangements.
questions.why: Raises supplier risk, national-security assessment and transparency in public-sector data-platform contracts.
questions.linkText: Written question 44199: Palantir contract exits in France, Switzerland and Germany

questions.title: NS&I's dependency on Atos and move to multi-supplier sourcing
questions.who: Siân Berry MP (Green Party, Brighton Pavilion)
questions.body: Berry asked about the risks of National Savings and Investments' technical/operational dependency on Atos. The Treasury confirmed NS&I is moving away from a single supplier, that Sopra Steria took over parts of Atos's role in April 2025, and that NS&I is increasing in-house capability. It said NS&I would continue to review and iterate its approach in line with the Government's new Public Interest Test on Insourcing.
questions.why: Describes a public body's move away from a single provider, increased in-house capability and review of its approach in line with the new Public Interest Test on Insourcing.
questions.linkText: Written question 45034: NS&I dependency on Atos

questions.title: Civil service pension questions and teachers' pension administration-transfer problems
questions.who: Euan Stainbank MP (Labour, Falkirk); Victoria Collins MP (Liberal Democrat, Harpenden and Berkhamsted); Caroline Voaden MP (Liberal Democrat, South Devon)
questions.where: Written questions — Cabinet Office; Department for Education
questions.body: Stainbank asked about the impact of Capita's update of 23 November on its Civil Service Pension Scheme contract, and about interest and compensation for delayed pension payments (uin 46093, 46094, 46367). Collins and Voaden separately asked about members of the Teachers' Pension Scheme unable to access the online portal, and about login failures and inaccurate records, following the transfer of administration from Capita to Tata Consultancy Services on 1 November (uin 46037, 46222).
questions.why: Seeks information on civil service pension payment delays and costs, and on access and records following the teachers' pension administration transfer.
questions.linkText: Written question 46093: Capita's Civil Service Pension Scheme contract

questions.title: MoD questions on Starlink alternatives and possible Starshield restrictions
questions.body: MacCleary asked which commercial alternatives to Starlink have been evaluated or deployed (uin 44129), and whether any roles would be affected by a possible speed restriction on UK Starshield terminals (uin 44130). The Minister said the MoD maintains a range of military and commercial satellite capabilities to reduce reliance on any single provider and support "strategic autonomy".
questions.why: Concerns resilience, supplier diversification and strategic autonomy in defence satellite communications.
questions.linkText: Written question 44129: commercial alternatives to Starlink

questions.title: Data Centre Covenant implementation questioned
questions.who: Luke Myer MP (Labour, Middlesbrough South and East Cleveland); Liz Twist MP (Labour, Blaydon and Consett); Lee Barron MP (Labour, Corby and East Northamptonshire)
questions.where: Written questions — Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade; Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
questions.body: Myer asked about minimum requirements for Local Benefit Plans under the Data Centre Covenant and whether network operators will have to publish data-centre grid-reinforcement costs (uin 43742, 43740). Twist asked how compute for public services will be secured under the Covenant (uin 46278). Barron asked about the timeline for identifying strategic data centres under the Covenant (uin 46313).
questions.why: Direct scrutiny of the Government's Data Centre Covenant, covering energy costs, compute access and community benefit — core to the data-centre/AI-infrastructure theme.
questions.linkText: Written question 43742: Data Centre Covenant Local Benefit Plans

questions.title: AI companies' adherence to copyright law questioned
questions.where: Written question — Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
questions.body: Lamb asked what steps the Department is taking to ensure AI companies adhere to copyright law.
questions.why: Raises AI companies' compliance with copyright law.
questions.linkText: Written question 46282: AI companies and copyright law

questions.title: Serco, Capita and G4S contract spend questioned across multiple departments
questions.who: Sir John Hayes MP (Conservative, South Holland and The Deepings); Andy McDonald MP (Labour, Middlesbrough and Thornaby East)
questions.where: Written questions — Department for Work and Pensions; Northern Ireland Office; Scotland Office; Wales Office
questions.body: Hayes tabled an identical question to several departments asking how much each has spent on contracts with Serco, Capita and G4S over the last three years (uin 40749 DWP, 46003 Northern Ireland Office, 46005 Scotland Office, 46012 Wales Office). McDonald separately asked DWP how many Capita contracts it holds, their total value, and what contingency arrangements exist for critical Capita performance failure (uin 43039, 43040, 43042). He also asked what criteria DWP uses to determine whether a contractor has experienced a critical performance failure (uin 43043).
questions.why: Raises departmental supplier-spending transparency and contingency planning for outsourced services.
questions.linkText: Written question 40749: DWP spend with Serco, Capita and G4S

questions.title: "Middle tech companies" and the CMA's digital markets regime
questions.who: Victoria Collins MP (Liberal Democrat, Harpenden and Berkhamsted)
questions.where: Written questions — Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
questions.body: Collins asked for an estimate of the number of "middle tech" companies in the UK and their economic contribution (uin 43836), and how the impact of the digital markets competition regime on companies competing with or depending on strategic-market-status firms is being assessed (uin 43837). The Government confirmed a post-implementation review of the regime is planned, typically three to five years after implementation.
questions.why: Concerns assessment of the competition regime's effects on firms that compete with or depend on companies designated with strategic market status.
questions.linkText: Written question 43836: middle tech companies in the UK

questions.title: AI data centres and local drinking-water supply
questions.where: Written question — Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
questions.body: Lord Taylor asked what steps are being taken to ensure new AI data centres do not strain local drinking-water supplies. The Government said developers are expected to minimise public water use and that new AI Growth Zone sites must demonstrate sufficient access to water, confirmed in writing by the relevant local supplier.
questions.why: Sets out water-use expectations for developers and the mandatory evidence of water access for new AI Growth Zone sites.
questions.linkText: Written question HL5274: AI data centres and drinking water
